evidence: A first reckoning, nothing in it observed. The thresholds and the flux law are published relations fitted on Earth and carried to lunar gravity; no experiment at 1.62 m/s2 in dense air tests them. The winds are 3-day means of the design climate's run at T21 (about 170 km), used as the run gives them, carried from its 2 m land roughness to a sand surface by a stated factor, with the unresolved part as a stated range from the two-dimensional cloud-resolving rings at 45 deg and the highland box. The supply (mantle, river ends, shores) and the holding (plants, crusts, damp) are brackets from the project's studies and from Earth's literature. The map is a screening scheme on the 1.9 km grid, not a transport model: it places the offered sand, carries it downwind as far as the drift allows in the land's age, fanning out where the winds vary, and stops it at shelter, cover and water. Areas are what the scheme gives for each stated case.
reading_rule: Grids are 2,880 rows from 90 N by 5,760 columns from 0 E, 16 per degree, on today's Moon (the design surface's grid). sand_share is the share of the cell's ground under loose sand (0 over water); active_share the share of that sand that is bare and moves within a year; form 0 none, 1 sheet or streaks (and sand on the floors of small bowls), 2 crescent dunes and transverse ridges, 3 linear dunes, 4 star dunes, 5 dunes held under plants or crust; crest_azimuth_deg the direction the crests run, clockwise from today's north, between 0 and 180 (NaN for forms 0, 1 and 4); crest_spacing_m the distance between crests (0 where no dunes); drift_azimuth_deg the direction the sand is carried towards, clockwise from today's north (NaN where nothing moves). These hold the central case; each variant has the same fields with the suffix __<variant>. Also kept: sand_thickness_m (the sand spread evenly over the cell, bulk metres); drift_potential_m2_yr (what all winds together could carry over bare loose sand, bulk m3 per metre of width a year, for the central case and for __nogust and __highgust), drift_resultant_m2_yr (the net of it, central) and drift_direction_deg (the direction that net travels, clockwise from today's north, on all land, central; NaN over water); basalt_share (the mare map's share of the rock under the cell), plant_cover (the globe's cover curve at the cell's aridity) and shelter (0 open, 1 in the lee of higher ground or on a floor).

pathways.note: the convergence is what a flux at the wind's capacity would lay down; the supply found here keeps the flux far below capacity

basis.note: a river end in the hyper-arid land at 70 deg (12 mm of rain a year) with the capped catchment, all its durable sand taken; a downwind sea shore; the median central drift potential over land

central.rests_on: the run's winds carried to sand, the unresolved part at the wet 45 deg rings' factor (1.3) with the storms' tail; crusts kept on arid and semi-arid sand as on other open ground; central supply; the land ten thousand years after it dried

nogust.rests_on: the central case on the run's 3-day means alone: no turbulence, no circulations below 170 km, no storms

highgust.rests_on: the central case with the unresolved part at the design-ground 45 deg rings' factor (2.0), storms twice as frequent and their gusts half again as strong

opensand.rests_on: the central case with crust upkeep absent from sand (dune fields, sheets, bowl floors, river-laid and shore sand) in the arid and semi-arid land; plants alone hold it

young.rests_on: the central case one thousand years after the land dried: a tenth of the rivers' and shores' sand, deeper bowls

ample.rests_on: the central case with every supply bracket at its high end: 0.2 m of mantle winnowed, seven tenths of the sand grains lasting, twice the erosion, mouths credited with 20,000 km2, shores offering 3 m3 a metre a year

limits: The winds are one run's, at 170 km and 3 days; sea and lake breezes, slope winds and the storms' gusts enter only through the stated factor and tail.
The cover is the globe's display curve at each cell's aridity; wetter ground along rivers and in hollows is left out.
Rivers' sand is credited by catchment behind each mouth with a cap; lakes upstream that hold sand back are not followed.
Shore sand is a bracket per metre of downwind shore; no wave or tide model stands behind it.

The carrying scheme moves sand along one direction per cell, each case's resultant, for at most 200 moves from cell to cell (380 km along a meridian); it fans out by a stated share at each move and is shared over 4.7 km at the end.

The climate's fields reach the 1.9 km grid smoothed over 0.7 of the run's 170 km spacing, as the round's look carries them: nothing in the map is finer than that except what the ground gives (water, shelter, river ends and shores).
Dune forms follow the resultant over the potential and the sand's thickness by Earth's classes; crest spacings are an estimate from the sand at hand and the time.
